stations.grain: one row per NEVI-funded station on PennDOT's roster (13 stations; 10 have session data in this release)

columns.name: station_id
columns.desc: EV-ChART station identifier (text). Join key for every other table

columns.name: awardee
columns.desc: NEVI awardee / site host (e.g. Pilot Travel Centers, Love's, Tesla Inc.)

columns.name: network_operator
columns.desc: Charging network: EVgo, ChargePoint, Tesla, Francis Energy

columns.name: station_name
columns.desc: Short town name used throughout the dashboard, e.g. 'Pittston'. Prefer this in answers

columns.name: n_ports
columns.desc: Number of charging ports (all stations have 4)

columns.name: has_session_data
columns.desc: FALSE for stations that opened after the data cut-off (Mifflinville, New Castle, Brookville)

daily_station.grain: one row per station per local calendar day (America/New_York), from opening through its last reported day; zero-session days included

columns.name: ports_used
columns.desc: Distinct ports with a successful session

columns.name: busy_port_minutes
columns.desc: Sum over ports of minutes occupied by a successful session

columns.name: all_ports_busy_minutes
columns.desc: Minutes in the day when every port was occupied (queue risk)

columns.name: outage_port_minutes
columns.desc: Sum over ports of reported outage minutes that day (no exclusions)

monthly_port.grain: one row per port per month from the station's opening month

columns.name: outage_minutes
columns.desc: Reported outage minutes (Module 4), split across days, no exclusions

columns.name: minutes_in_service
columns.desc: Minutes the port was in service this month (partial first month)

columns.name: uptime_pct
columns.desc: Raw monthly availability = 100*(1 - outage_minutes/minutes_in_service). Does NOT apply NEVI excluded outages, so it is a conservative lower bound

port_uptime_reported.grain: one row per port: the latest cumulative Module 3 uptime report

columns.name: reported_uptime_pct
columns.desc: Operator-reported 12-month uptime; NULL when the port has < 1 year of history

columns.name: excluded_outage_min
columns.desc: Outage minutes excluded under 23 CFR 680.116 (utility outage, vandalism, etc.)

columns.name: uptime_since_start_pct
columns.desc: 100*(1 - (total_outage_min - excluded_outage_min)/minutes since reporting_start). NEVI formula applied to the whole period since the port's first report

columns.name: uptime_nevi_pct
columns.desc: Compliance figure to use: the operator-reported 12-month uptime when available, otherwise uptime_since_start_pct

outage_events.grain: one row per reported outage event per port

quarterly_station.grain: one row per station per quarter, computed from the raw submissions by this pipeline

columns.name: sessions_per_day
columns.desc: Successful sessions per day in service

columns.name: uptime_pct_raw
columns.desc: Raw quarterly availability across all ports, no exclusions

quarterly_reported.grain: one row per station per quarter, exactly as reported in PennDOT's quarterly summary workbook

hourly_profile.grain: successful sessions by station, quarter, day of week, and local start hour

failures_quarterly.grain: failed sessions by station, quarter, and failure type

columns.name: failure_type
columns.desc: ChargeX error code (CX002, CX009, ...), 'other', 'Corrupted', or 'no_error_but_<1kWh' (session ended with no error code but delivered < 1 kWh)

payments_quarterly.grain: successful sessions by station, quarter, and payment method

columns.name: payment_method
columns.desc: credit_card_terminal, phone_online, membership, roaming, other, none

session_distribution.grain: histogram of successful sessions per station; one row per (station, metric, bin)

columns.name: is_top_bin
columns.desc: TRUE for the last bin, which also holds every value above it

rules: Data covers 2023-12-22 to 2025-03-31 (EV-ChART quarterly submissions through 2025 Q1). Say so if a question asks about later dates.
Successful session = no error code AND >= 1 kWh delivered. Failed = everything else.

NEVI uptime requirement (23 CFR 680.116): each port >= 97% over a trailing 12 months, with excluded outages removed. Use port_uptime_reported.uptime_nevi_pct for compliance; monthly_port.uptime_pct is a raw lower bound.
NEVI minimum power: 150 kW per port simultaneously. Session power is limited by the vehicle as well as the charger, so median session power below 150 kW is NOT by itself a violation.
Tesla (Aston) reports zero failed sessions - Tesla's submission appears not to include failures; flag this when comparing reliability.
Scales: *_pct columns are 0-100 (97% is written 97, never 0.97); *_rate columns and port_utilization are 0-1 fractions.
Always join to stations to show station_name; never show raw station_id alone.
Quarters are strings like '2025Q1'. Months are timestamps at the first of the month.
Session-level records are NOT available - only these aggregates. Do not invent columns.

examples.q: Which ports are below the 97% uptime requirement?
examples.sql:
SELECT s.station_name, p.port_label, p.uptime_nevi_pct, p.reporting_start, p.reporting_end
FROM port_uptime_reported p JOIN stations s USING (station_id)
WHERE p.uptime_nevi_pct < 97 ORDER BY p.uptime_nevi_pct
SELECT month, SUM(sessions_success) AS sessions FROM daily_station GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

examples.q: What are the main failure causes at Francis Energy stations?
examples.sql:
SELECT s.station_name, f.failure_type, SUM(f.sessions) AS sessions
FROM failures_quarterly f JOIN stations s USING (station_id)
WHERE s.network_operator = 'Francis Energy' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY s.station_name, sessions DESC

examples.q: Busiest hour of the week at Aston
examples.sql:
SELECT day_of_week, hour, SUM(sessions) AS sessions FROM hourly_profile h JOIN stations s USING (station_id)
WHERE s.station_name = 'Aston' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY sessions DESC LIMIT 5
